h1:
Getting Around Satun
How to Arrive and Reach the Islands
intro: Satun has no airport of its own, so most people fly into Hat Yai first, then catch a van to Pak Bara Pier, the main gateway to Koh Lipe and Koh Tarutao. It sounds like a lot of connections, but switching from plane to van to boat is easier than it looks. We've pulled together the routes, real prices, van and boat schedules, and the road links over to Trang, all in one place.
chips: ✈️ Land at Hat Yai, van to Pak Bara

blocks.html: The first thing to understand is that Satun has no airport. The nearest airport with the most flights is Hat Yai (in Songkhla province); from there you take a van into Satun town or straight to Pak Bara Pier to catch a boat to the islands. The trip breaks down into three main legs: getting to Satun (plane + van), reaching the islands from Pak Bara Pier (boats to Koh Lipe/Tarutao), and road links to neighbouring provinces like Trang. Get the order right and the connections flow smoothly, with no need to overnight in Hat Yai.

blocks.text: Fly into Hat Yai first, then how to continue

blocks.html: Hat Yai Airport (HDY) has several flights a day from Bangkok (Don Mueang/Suvarnabhumi), on both budget and full-service carriers. Once you land, there are two main choices: head into Satun town first, or go straight to Pak Bara Pier for the islands. The distance from Hat Yai Airport to Pak Bara is around 2 hours, depending on traffic and weather.

items.name: Van straight to Pak Bara — if you're heading to the islands right away
items.blurb: The most popular option for Koh Lipe/Tarutao travellers. Vans and transfer services run from Hat Yai Airport directly to Pak Bara Pier, taking around 2 hours. The scheduled Hat Yai-Pak Bara van costs about 120 THB, while a pre-booked airport pickup runs from around 250 THB per person. Best if you plan to reach the islands the same day.
items.meta: ~2 hrs · 120 THB (scheduled) to ~250 THB+ (booked airport pickup)

items.name: Van into Satun town — if you want to stay in town first
items.blurb: If you're not rushing to the islands, or you want to explore Satun town, visit the Kuden Mansion museum, Mambang Mosque, or eat seafood in town first, take the Hat Yai-Satun van into town. Fares start at around 120-250 THB, and the Hat Yai-Satun distance is about 96 km. Then catch a ride on to Pak Bara the next morning.

items.name: Private car/taxi from the airport — for groups with lots of luggage
items.blurb: Travelling as a family, with small kids, or hauling heavy bags for diving? A private car from Hat Yai Airport straight to Pak Bara is more comfortable, with no waiting for van departures. The fare is negotiable but usually runs in the low thousands of THB per trip for a sedan or van. Agree on the price and drop-off point clearly before you set off.

blocks.title: Time your arrival to catch the last boat
blocks.html: The last boat to Koh Lipe usually leaves in the afternoon. If your flight lands in Hat Yai around midday and you still have a 2-hour van ride, you may miss the afternoon boat. Go for a morning flight, or plan to overnight near Pak Bara/La-ngu and take the morning boat the next day for peace of mind.

blocks.text: Hat Yai-Pak Bara vans: schedules, prices, pickup points

blocks.html: The Hat Yai-Pak Bara van is the lifeline for travellers heading to the islands. Bus companies run regular services throughout the day, and you can usually board without booking ahead on a weekday. But in high season or on long weekends it gets busy, so booking ahead or arriving early gives more peace of mind.

items: Fare — the scheduled Hat Yai-Pak Bara van is around 120 THB per person; an online-booked airport pickup runs higher, from around 250 THB.
Schedule — from Hat Yai, the first van leaves around 06:00 and the last around 19:00, roughly every 30 minutes · from Pak Bara, the first leaves around 06:15 and the last around 17:00.
Travel time — usually around 1.5-2 hours, but heavy rain or traffic can stretch it to 3 hours, so always allow extra time.

Pickup points in Hat Yai — there are both in-town van stands in Hat Yai and airport pickup services. Confirm clearly with the Satun van stand at the bus terminal, or with the operator you booked, exactly where they pick up.

blocks.text: Pak Bara Pier — Satun's gateway to the islands

blocks.html: Pak Bara Pier, in La-ngu district, is the main pier where boats depart for Koh Lipe, Koh Tarutao, Koh Khai, and the other islands in Tarutao National Park. There's a pier-use fee of 20 THB per person. Arrive at least 30 minutes before your boat leaves to check in, get your boat company's wristband, and load your luggage in time.

blocks.title: What many people get wrong at Pak Bara
blocks.html: Boat tickets are usually sold as round-trip packages. If you buy one-way first and plan to buy the return on the island, the price can be higher at certain times and seats fill up fast. We recommend buying the round trip with one company and keeping your wristband safe, since it doubles as your return ticket.

blocks.text: Pak Bara → Koh Lipe: how to get there and what it costs

blocks.html: Koh Lipe is Satun's most popular destination, reached by speedboat from Pak Bara in around 1.5 hours (add about half an hour if the boat stops at Koh Tarutao/Koh Khai along the way). Koh Lipe has no large pier, so the speedboat anchors offshore and a longtail boat ferries you to the beach. The beach-transfer fare is usually included in package tickets.

items.name: Round-trip speedboat, Pak Bara-Koh Lipe
items.blurb: The standard option for travellers. A round-trip speedboat ticket including the beach transfer is around 900-1,000 THB per person (it drops to about 900 THB in parts of the low season). Companies people use often include Akira Speed Boat and Ploysiam Speedboat; you can book online in advance, with a deposit of around 300 THB and the rest paid on the day.
items.meta: ~1.5 hrs · round trip ~900-1,000 THB (incl. beach transfer)

items.name: Main boat departures
items.blurb: Pak Bara-Koh Lipe speedboats run several times a day. The most consistent departures are 09:30, 11:30, and 13:30. Some run direct, others stop at Koh Tarutao/Koh Khai along the way. Late-afternoon departures may be suspended in some seasons, so always check times with the boat company before you plan, especially outside high season.

items.name: Van + boat package from Hat Yai
items.blurb: If you'd rather not arrange the van and boat connections yourself, many operators sell a combined package: a van pickup from Hat Yai Airport plus a round-trip boat to Koh Lipe, all in one. Convenient for first-timers. The total price depends on the pickup point and season; ask the operator about pickup times and the boat connection before booking.
items.meta: Combined van + boat · price varies by pickup/season

blocks.text: Pak Bara → Koh Tarutao: how to get there and park fees

blocks.html: Koh Tarutao is a large island in Tarutao National Park, much closer to Pak Bara than Koh Lipe. The speedboat from Pak Bara takes around 30 minutes. It suits both day-trippers and those who want to overnight in the park's bungalows or campground. The atmosphere is quieter than Koh Lipe, with a focus on nature and the history of the old prison.

items: Boats to Tarutao — usually a 11:30 departure, with a 14:30 added in high season; the trip takes around 30 minutes from Pak Bara. The Tarutao-Pak Bara return often has just one mid-morning departure, around 10:30. Always check with the boat company.
Tarutao National Park fee — around 40 THB for Thais, around 220 THB for foreigners (children pay reduced rates), paid on arrival at the island.
Pak Bara pier fee — 20 THB per person, the same as on every boat.
Overnight stays — Tarutao has park bungalows and a campground, booked in advance through the national park's system. They fill up fast in high season.

blocks.title: The park closes in monsoon season
blocks.html: Tarutao National Park and the islands around here usually close during the monsoon, roughly mid-May to mid-October. Some boat services stop running or reduce departures. If you're planning a rainy-season trip, check the national park's announcements and the boat companies before booking anything.

blocks.text: Road links to Trang and neighbouring provinces

blocks.html: Satun pairs easily with Trang, and many people combine both into a single Satun-Trang trip, or fly into Trang and enter Satun from there. Here are the rough distances and times between the main connection points. Always allow extra time when it rains, since the southern roads get slick and traffic slows down.

items: Hat Yai → Satun — about 96 km, around 1.5-2 hours by van, with fares starting at around 120 THB.
Hat Yai → Trang — the van takes around 2.5 hours, fares around 120-130 THB; it's a route travellers linking the two provinces use often.
Trang → Satun (town) — around 1.5 hours by van, fares around 120-150 THB, handy for visiting both provinces together.
Trang has an airport — if you can find a flight into Trang, you can use it as a southern gateway into Satun too. Choose based on airfares and flight times.

items: Avoid monsoon season if you want to dive — roughly mid-May to mid-October brings strong winds and waves, with parts of the park closed and fewer boats. The popular high season is November to April.
Allow time for the van and boat connections — southern vans depend on traffic and rain, so don't book a boat that cuts it too close. Leave at least an hour's buffer for van delays.
Carry cash — pier fees, park fees, and many island shops take cash mainly. ATMs on Koh Lipe are few and charge high fees.
Keep your boat wristband safe — boat companies use wristband colours to mark your departure and return. Lose it and you may waste time re-confirming your identity.
Always check boat times beforehand — schedules change with the season and weather. Call or message the boat company to confirm departures before you actually set off.

faq.q: Which airport do I fly into for Satun?
faq.a: Satun has no airport of its own. Most people fly into Hat Yai Airport (in Songkhla province), which has several flights a day from Bangkok, then take a van into Satun town or to Pak Bara Pier. Another option is flying into Trang Airport and continuing into Satun from the south.

faq.q: How long does it take from Hat Yai Airport to Pak Bara Pier, and how much?
faq.a: It takes around 2 hours, depending on traffic and weather. The scheduled Hat Yai-Pak Bara van is about 120 THB per person, while a booked airport pickup straight to the pier runs from around 250 THB. From Hat Yai, the first van leaves around 06:00 and the last around 19:00, roughly every 30 minutes.

faq.q: What are the boat departures from Pak Bara to Koh Lipe, and how much?
faq.a: The main speedboat departures are 09:30, 11:30, and 13:30, with a trip of around 1.5 hours. A round-trip ticket including the beach transfer is around 900-1,000 THB per person, plus a 20 THB Pak Bara pier fee per person. Always check times with the boat company first, since schedules change with the season.

faq.q: How do I get to Koh Tarutao from Pak Bara, and what fees apply?
faq.a: Take a speedboat from Pak Bara, around 30 minutes. There's usually a 11:30 departure, with a 14:30 added in high season; the return often has just one mid-morning departure, around 10:30. The Tarutao National Park fee is around 40 THB for Thais and around 220 THB for foreigners, plus a 20 THB Pak Bara pier fee per person.

faq.q: How far is Hat Yai to Trang, and Trang to Satun?
faq.a: Hat Yai-Trang is around 2.5 hours by van, with fares around 120-130 THB, while Trang-Satun town is around 1.5 hours, with fares around 120-150 THB. It's ideal for anyone wanting to combine Satun and Trang in a single trip.
